acc.title: Who can open {{name}}
acc.lede: This covers the computer's programs opened through their web addresses: terminal, files, display and the others.
acc.now.anyone: Now: anyone with a program's address can open it.
acc.now.myIp: Now: only connections from {{ip}} can open the programs.
acc.now.ips: Now: only connections from {{ips}} can open the programs.
acc.now.ipsMany: Now: only connections from the {{n}} addresses listed below can open the programs.
acc.now.private: Now: private. Nobody can open the programs through their addresses.
acc.now.advanced: Now: rules set outside the Hub decide who can open the programs.
acc.anyoneHelp: No sign-in. Anyone who has a program's address, or is sent it, can open that program.
acc.myIpHelp: Only connections from the address you are using now. Anyone else with the link is turned away.
acc.ipsHelp: Only connections from the addresses you list: yours, an office, a range. Anyone else with the link is turned away.
acc.ips.label: Allowed IPv4 addresses or ranges
acc.ips.err.ipv6: {{entry}} is IPv6. Access rules take IPv4 only.
acc.ips.err.host_bits: {{entry}} isn't a whole range. Write its first address.
acc.ips.err.all: {{entry}} is every address, so it keeps nobody out. Remove it.
acc.people: Only people or keys I pick
acc.peopleHelp: Each person signs in with a name and password, or opens a link that carries a key. Everyone else is kept out.
acc.privateHelp: Nobody can open the programs through their addresses, you included. A link someone already has stops working.
acc.ipChanged: The address you use now changed since it was shown. What's shown now is your current address: check it, then press Save again.
acc.ipChangedSame: The address you use now changed since it was shown. It is the address these rules already allow, so there is nothing to save.
acc.ipNote: Access rules take IPv4 addresses only.
acc.ipv6: You're connected over IPv6 ({{ip}}). Access rules take IPv4 addresses only, so this choice can't let you in from this connection. A network with IPv4 can.
acc.ipOdd: The address the Hoody API sees ({{ip}}) isn't one an access rule can take.
acc.lockout: If your IP address changes (another Wi-Fi, mobile data, a VPN), the programs stop opening for you. You can still change this rule in the Hub from any network, once signed in: it doesn't apply to the Hub or the Hoody API.
acc.ips.lockout: Access rules take IPv4 addresses only. From an address that is not in the list, the programs do not open for you either. You can still change this rule in the Hub from any network, once signed in: it doesn't apply to the Hub or the Hoody API.
acc.adv.lede: These rules were set outside the Hub, with the API or another tool. The Hub shows them and leaves them as they are.
sum.anyone: Anyone with a program's address can open it.
sum.anyoneGroups: Everyone not in a group is let in, unless a password group below asks for sign-in on that program.
sum.only_one: Only members of {{groups}} can open the programs, and only what its rule allows. Everyone else is kept out.
sum.only_other: Only members of {{groups}} can open the programs, each only what its rule allows. Everyone else is kept out.
sum.nobody: Nobody can open the programs through their addresses.
sum.noDefault: The rules don't say what happens to everyone not in a group.
sum.offProject: The project switches its computers' web addresses off: a computer that doesn't switch them on itself can't be opened through them.
sum.off: The programs' web addresses are switched off for this computer: nobody can open them.
sum.projectToo: Its project has access rules too. They can let more people in, ask for a password, or switch the addresses off, so these rules alone don't tell who gets in.
sum.projectUnknown: The Hub can't tell whether its project has access rules too. If it has, they can let more people in, ask for a password, or switch the addresses off.
sum.hooks_one: {{count}} hook is set up. It runs on the visits it matches.
sum.hooks_other: {{count}} hooks are set up. Each runs on the visits it matches.
acc.confirm.title: Change who can open {{name}}'s programs?
acc.confirm.anyone: Anyone who has a program's address will be able to open it, with no sign-in. That includes anyone you've sent a link to, or who finds one.
acc.confirm.myIp: Only connections from {{ip}} will open the programs. Anyone else with a link is turned away. If your address changes (another Wi-Fi, mobile data, a VPN), they stop opening for you too, until you change this here in the Hub.
acc.confirm.ips: Only connections from {{ips}} will open the programs. Anyone else with a link is turned away.
acc.confirm.ips.ended: The people and keys set here ({{n}}) are removed and can no longer open the programs.
acc.confirm.ips.out: Your address now, {{ip}}, is not in the list: the programs will stop opening for you until you change this here in the Hub.
acc.confirm.ips.v6: You're connected over IPv6 now. Access rules take IPv4 only, so the programs will not open for you from this connection.
acc.confirm.ips.unknown: The Hub couldn't read your address now, so it can't tell whether the programs will still open for you.
acc.confirm.private: Nobody will open the programs through their addresses, you included. Links people already have stop working. You can change this here in the Hub at any time.
acc.held.anyone: Your change to “Anyone with the address” may have gone through, or may still be on its way. Check again reads the rules; it never sends the change again.
acc.held.myIp: Your change to “Only my IP” may have gone through, or may still be on its way. Check again reads the rules; it never sends the change again.
acc.held.ips: Your change to “Only these IPs” may have gone through, or may still be on its way. Check again reads the rules; it never sends the change again.
acc.held.private: Your change to “Private” may have gone through, or may still be on its way. Check again reads the rules; it never sends the change again.
acc.held.other: A change to these rules may have gone through, or may still be on its way. Check again reads the rules; it never sends the change again.
acc.held.dismissBody: Stop tracking only if you're sure it didn't go through. If it did, the rules have already changed, and saving again over the old ones is refused.
acc.held.dismissBodyOn: Only if you're sure the change to {{name}} didn't go through. If it did, the rules have already changed, and saving over the old ones is refused.
acc.stale: These rules were changed somewhere else after this page read them. Nothing was changed here.
acc.saved: Saved. The rules now read as you chose.
acc.moved: Saved, but the rules now read differently: they may have been changed somewhere else since. What's shown is what applies now.
acc.adv.cantChange: The Hub can't change these rules here without losing the ones it doesn't show.
acc.adv.how: Change them with the Hoody API
acc.explain.unknown: The question may have reached the Agent. Its answer, if any, is in the Agent panel: asking again opens it instead of asking twice.
acc.explain.notSent: The question didn't reach the Agent. You can ask again.
acc.movedUnknown: The rules now read differently from what you chose: they were changed somewhere else, so it isn't known whether your change went through first. What's shown is what applies now.
acc.explain.unread: The rules couldn't be read, so nothing was sent to the Agent. Try again.
acc.now.people: Now: only the people and key links listed below can open the programs.
acc.held.step: A step of your change may have gone through, or may still be on its way. Check again reads the rules; it never sends that step again.
acc.p.none: No people or key links yet. Add the first one: everyone else is then kept out.
acc.p.title: People and key links
acc.p.col.name: Name
acc.p.addOff.secret: Press Done on the password or link first.
acc.p.addOff.form: Finish or cancel the form first.
acc.p.person: Person, signs in with a password
acc.p.keyOnce: The link was shown once, when the key was made. To share it again, remove the key and make a new one.
acc.p.name: Name
acc.p.nameHelpPerson: They type this name when they sign in. Letters and numbers; spaces become dashes.
acc.p.nameHelpKey: Only for you, to tell keys apart.
acc.p.nameBad: Use letters or numbers, up to 32 characters.
acc.p.nameTaken: There's already one with this name.
acc.p.allHelp: Also programs added to the computer later.
acc.p.logs: Logs (never included in the programs above)
acc.p.confirmPerson: {{name}} will open the programs you picked after signing in with their name and a password the Hub makes now. You'll see the password once: copy it and send it to them yourself.
acc.p.confirmKey: Anyone who has this link can open the programs you picked, with no sign-in. The key is part of the link. So it can show up in browser history, in logs of visited addresses, and in the Referer header sent to other sites the program links to. Share it only with people who should have it. To take access away, remove the key here. Every link with it then stops working.
acc.p.confirmAddrGo: Connections from {{ips}} will no longer get in by address alone.
acc.p.confirmKeepOut: Everyone else, including anyone who has a program's address, will be kept out.
acc.p.removePerson: {{name}} won't be able to sign in any more.
acc.p.removeKey: Every link with this key stops working.
acc.p.removeLast: It's the last one: after it, nobody can open the programs through their addresses (Private).
acc.p.unfinishedOpen: An earlier change here stopped partway: anyone with a program's address can still open the programs.
acc.p.unfinishedNothing: An earlier change here stopped partway: {{names}} can open nothing yet. Remove it and add it again.
acc.p.finishBody: Only the people and key links listed will open the programs. Anyone else with a program's address is turned away.
acc.p.resumeHelp: Some steps of your change aren't in place yet. Finish adding sends only those, checked against the rules as they read now.
acc.p.secretMaybe: It isn't known yet whether this was saved. Keep it until the rules show it.
acc.p.stale: The rules changed somewhere else, so that step wasn't saved. What's shown is what applies now; steps that went through stay.
acc.p.refused: That step wasn't saved. Steps that went through stay.
acc.p.unread: The answer didn't show that step. What's shown is a fresh read of the rules.
acc.now.peopleMyIp: Now: the people and key links listed below, and connections from the address Only my IP named, can open the programs.
acc.now.peopleIps: Now: the people and key links listed below, and connections from the addresses Only these IPs named, can open the programs.
acc.now.cut: Now: an earlier add stopped partway. Only entries listed with programs can open them.
acc.now.cutMyIp: Now: an earlier add stopped partway. The address from Only my IP, and entries listed with programs, can open the programs.
acc.now.cutIps: Now: an earlier add stopped partway. The addresses from Only these IPs, and entries listed with programs, can open the programs.
acc.p.unfinishedMyIp: An earlier add stopped before the address from Only my IP was removed: that address still gets in. Keep everyone else out removes it.
acc.p.unfinishedIps: An earlier add stopped before the addresses from Only these IPs were removed: those addresses still get in. Keep everyone else out removes them.
acc.p.unreadWait: The API said that step was saved, but no read of the rules has shown it yet. Nothing more is sent until one does.
acc.p.pickOneKey: Pick at least one program: a key link opens a program's address.
acc.p.removePersonOpen: After {{name}} is removed, anyone with the address can still open the programs: an earlier add stopped before everyone else was kept out.
acc.p.removeKeyOpen: After the key is removed, the programs still open for anyone with their address, the key’s links included, because an earlier add stopped partway.
acc.p.heldWait: You stopped tracking a step whose result wasn’t confirmed, so it may still go through. Nothing else is sent until the rules show a change made after that step was sent.
acc.p.removeMyIp: After it is removed, connections from the address Only my IP named still get in: an earlier add stopped before that address was removed.
acc.p.removeIps: After it is removed, connections from the addresses Only these IPs named still get in: an earlier add stopped before those addresses were removed.
acc.p.noAddress: None of these programs has an address yet, so there's no link to give. Add a person instead, or try again once the computer has an address.
acc.change: Tell the Agent what you want
acc.changeHelp: Example: only my office IP can open the terminal. The Agent gets your request and these rules, without passwords or keys. It asks you to approve each change. It can't add passwords or key links: use Only people or keys I pick for those.
acc.change.long: Keep it to {{max}} characters or fewer.
acc.change.secret: This has a long run that mixes letters and digits, so it may be a password or key, and it isn't sent. Take it out: the Agent never needs one.
acc.change.watching: While this tab is open, it reads the rules again every few seconds to show what the Agent changed.
acc.change.moved: The rules changed after you asked the Agent. They are shown as they read now.
acc.proj.title: Where these rules come from
acc.proj.own.present: This computer keeps its own answer for everyone not in a group and inherits the project's groups and rules.
acc.proj.own.missing: This computer has no rules of its own: the project's rules decide alone.
acc.proj.own.unknown: The Hub couldn't read whether this computer has rules of its own. If it has, it keeps its own answer for everyone not in a group and inherits the project's groups and rules; if not, the project's rules decide alone.
acc.proj.use.title: Use only the project's rules
acc.proj.use.body: Removes this computer's own rules. The project's rules then decide alone. Right now they say:
acc.proj.use.readFailed: Couldn't read the rules again, so nothing was changed. Try again.
acc.proj.use.confirm.title: Remove this computer's own rules?
acc.proj.use.confirm.body: {{name}} will follow only the rules of {{project}}, as they are when this takes effect. Right now they say: {{summary}} Its own groups, people and keys stop applying here, unless the project gives the same people a way in.
acc.proj.use.done: Done. {{name}} has no rules of its own now and follows {{project}}'s rules. The addresses change after a delay.
acc.proj.use.again: Its own rules were removed, and rules of its own were written again since, somewhere else.
acc.proj.use.unproved: Removed. Reading it back failed, so the Hub can't yet say it follows only the project. Check again reads it.
acc.proj.use.held: Removing may have gone through, or may still be on its way. Check again reads the rules; it never sends it again.
acc.proj.use.stillThere: Its own rules are still there; the change may still arrive.
acc.proj.use.newer: Rules of its own are there, written after your change was sent (or read before it arrived). Check again, or Stop tracking if you know they changed elsewhere.
acc.proj.parentChanged: The project's rules changed while this was open. Read the new rules before you confirm.
acc.proj.use.failed: Nothing was removed: the Hoody API refused it.
acc.proj.use.notSent: Nothing was sent, so nothing was removed. Try again.
acc.agent.subject: access to {{name}}
acc.agent.allTitle: Check who can open these computers
acc.agent.allSummary: The Agent writes one line per computer saying who can open its programs, then up to three risks. It changes nothing.
acc.agent.allContextRow: Access rules of {{count}} computers in this realm
acc.agent.allContextRow_one: Access rules of {{count}} computer in this realm
acc.agent.allReads: Read just now, and read again when you press Ask the Agent, so the Agent gets the rules as they are then. Passwords and keys are left out and ids are masked.
acc.agent.allSkipped: Only the first {{count}} computers are read; {{skipped}} more are not.
acc.agent.partLeft: What was left out to keep this short
acc.agent.left: Passwords and keys are left out and ids are masked.
acc.agent.oneSummary: The Agent explains who can open this computer's programs and from where, what is blocked, and anything risky. It changes nothing.
acc.agent.projectTitle: Explain who can open the computers of {{name}}
acc.agent.projectContext: the project's access rules and its {{count}} computers
acc.agent.projectContext_one: the project's access rules and its {{count}} computer
acc.agent.none: There is no computer to read access from.
acc.change.busy: A change to these rules is still out. Wait for it to settle.
acc.adv.why: Why can't I change these here?
acc.adv.more: More on who can open a computer
acc.p.noLinks: No address to link to yet: {{programs}}.
acc.p.continueOff: Give it a name and pick what it can open first.
perm.who.title: Who can open its programs
perm.why.none: No access rules keep anyone out.
perm.why.hereAnyone: Chosen here: {{name}}'s own rules let everyone in.
perm.why.unfinished: An earlier change stopped partway: see People and key links below.
perm.why.proxyOff: Its web addresses are switched off.
perm.why.hooks: Its rules run hooks on visits.
perm.why.rules: Its rules were written with the Hoody API or another tool.
perm.why.project: Its project has access rules too.
perm.why.projectUnknown: The Hub can't tell whether its project has access rules too.
perm.why.listed: This is what the computers list last showed. The rules themselves can't be read here.
perm.refused: This sign-in can't read {{name}}'s access rules from here. If you own its project, switch to All realms and open it again.
perm.cant: This sign-in can't read access rules. Sign in with your account, or use an access key that may manage access.
perm.expired: {{name}} has expired. Its access rules can be read but not changed.
perm.reinstalled: The server {{name}} ran on was reinstalled, so nothing of it runs any more. Its access rules can't be changed.
perm.secretOnce: Shown once. Copy it now: it can't be shown again.
acc.p.secretClose: Close? The password or link won't be shown again.
perm.project.title: Project
perm.project.lede: The project decides who can manage {{name}}: start and stop it, open its files, change these rules.
perm.project.name: Project
perm.project.people.key: Shown when you sign in with your account
perm.project.rules.yes: The project has access rules. They apply to this computer too.
perm.project.rules.no: None. Only this computer's own rules decide.
perm.project.missing: This computer's project isn't listed here.
perm.realms.title: Realms
perm.fw.title: Firewall
perm.fw.lede: The firewall decides which network traffic reaches {{name}} at all, SSH and other ports included. A visit must pass both.
perm.fw.gone: {{name}} is no longer on a server, so no traffic reaches it.
perm.fw.cant: This sign-in can't read firewall rules.
perm.how.title: How access works
perm.how.short: Access rules decide who opens the programs' web addresses. Who manages the computer, and its firewall, are separate.
perm.how.docs: Access rules in the API docs
